title: SPROUTS FARMERS MARKET
intro: At Meaningful Works, the client I have worked with the most has been Sprouts Farmers Market. My work with Sprouts Farmers Market emphasizes the handmade and quirky spirit of the brand. I've been fortunate to create OOH design, in-store displays, art direct and create assets for campaigns, and even create animated social posts. This page displays some work created for Sprouts Farmers Market. Creative Directors: Summer Woodward and Hunter Somerville Design assistance: Kristy Toyoda, Chantal Herrera, Jamie Back, Spencer Fraye Photography: Jason Travis

paragraph: During my time as a designer at Meaningful Works, this was a question that we commonly found ourselves asking. Through various projects, Sprouts Farmers Market always emphasized the importance of connecting their brand with delicious fresh food. Our concern was how do you make “fresh”, a commonly used term in grocery and restaurants, into something that consumers perceive as unique to the Sprouts brand.

Our solution came about showing fresh not just through imagery, but also through a fresh attitude. We leaned into the feeling of discovery and joyful note taking, known as Sprouts’ “forager spirit”. By embracing this brand attitude, freshness could be exciting, organic, and energizing. While other grocers claim they're fresh, they can't match the feeling of fresh that we are able to display in our work for Sprouts.

title: CORITA ART CENTER
intro: In the Fall of 2024, I was fortunate enough to be hired as a Gallery Assistant at Corita Art Center. While I originally helped with various tasks, my role evolved into creating graphic assets for the organization. This involved everything from social posts, to signage, to children's' educational worksheets. My proudest work is "break bread", a zine created for a Corita Art Center benefit dinner. The design for the zine was inspired from the "irregular bulletin", a student-made newsletter that was created during Corita Kent's tenure at Immaculate Heart College.

paragraph: Corita Art Center is an institution and gallery space that preserves and promotes the art, teachings, and passion for social justice of pop artist Corita Kent. In 2024, I was brought onto the Corita Art Center team and have been assisting with various projects since.

Through my time with Corita Art Center, I've had the opportunity to make social media assets, material for the gallery space, merchandise, and even a zine for a benefit dinner. I always found a significant challenge for designing for Corita Art Center was how to reference Corita Kent without being too literal to her work. I realized that the best way to reference Corita Kent was to use her philosophies on art making in my design work.

During Corita's time as the head of the art department at Immaculate Heart College, her and her students created a list of rules for the department, commonly called the "Ten Rules". I always took rule nine to heart when designing for Corita Art Center.
"Be happy whenever you can manage it. Enjoy yourself. It's lighter than you think."

title: SoCAL EARTH
intro: SoCal Earth is a brand and visual identity project created for the Robert Redford Conservancy for Southern California Sustainability at Pitzer College. SoCal Earth is a new environmental data website and educational program. My role with SoCal Earth was to create its visual identity and enhance its brand. When interviewing the Robert Redford Conservancy, the concept of living off what we already have kept emerging. With this resourceful philosophy in mind, I used the paper I already had in my studio to create the logo. Illustrations, animations, and even a cartoon mascot were all created with paper in my studio and then digitally converted to use on the site. For the final SoCal Earth experience, visit the site here .

paragraph: SoCal Earth is an environmental data program created by the Robert Redford Conservancy at Pitzer College. The conservancy requested that I design the visual identity for this new program, which was to launch as a website first. Besides appealing to Southern Californians, the conservancy emphasized the importance of communication resourcefulness through design.

When thinking of how to create a visual identity around an abstraction like "resourcefulness", I decided to make the abstraction more literal. Seeing that I had loose pieces of construction paper in my studio, I cut the logo and illustrations out of these pieces of paper. I was designing SoCal Earth around one of its main philosophies; using what we already have available to us.

Tons of collages of cut paper and pencil drawings were digitized, cleaned and polished, and made into the graphics for SoCal Earth. This held true for all the graphics on the site, as well as the kid's Burrowing Owl mascot, Ollie. To get the full experience, visit socalearth.org

title: CULTURAL OLYMPIAD POSTER
intro: In Spring of 2024, the cities of Paris, France and Los Angeles announced a poster competition for the Paris 2024 and Los Angeles 2028 Olympic and Paralympic games. The invitation to compete was given to three Los Angeles-area schools (ArtCenter College of Design, CalArts, and Otis College of Art and Design) and one Paris-based school (EPSAA: École Professionnelle Supérieure d'Arts graphiques de la Ville de Paris). Students were tasked to create a poster and social media animation that celebrated the Olympic and Paralympic games being held in Paris 2024 and the transition to Los Angeles 2028. Using my love of analog design, I created cut paper designs of the Eiffel Tower, an Olympic torch, and an Academy Award; symbols of the cities and the Olympic games. I'm happy say that my work was one of the entries chosen by the cites of Paris and Los Angeles. My work and other winning posters were displayed along the Canal Saint-Martin in Paris and on the City of Paris's website and social media for the 2024 games. The posters will then be displayed again in 2028 for the Los Angeles games. This project was also given a student bronze from the World Brand Design Society.

paragraph: This was a question that plagued me when I was designing a poster for the Paris 2024 Cultural Olympiad. In Spring of 2024, I entered a student contest to design a poster and animation celebrating the transition of the Summer Olympics from Paris in 2024 to Los Angeles in 2028. This was a contest held between three art schools in the Los Angeles area and one in Paris. Despite the cities of Paris and Los Angeles feeling radically different, I had to design something that unified them.

When thinking of these cities, I realized both were massive tourist cities. With tourist cities come cheap souvenir stores. I saw that I could highlight these two cities by elevating plastic Eiffel Towers and faux Academy Awards into symbols of pride. Using a unifying mid-century cut paper style, an Eiffel Tower, an Olympic torch, and an Academy Award were combined to create a poster of transition between cities.

title: VALLEY STRONG CREDIT UNION
intro: During my time at Meaningful Works, I've had the opportunity to work on multiple projects for Valley Strong Credit Union. The largest of these projects was creating a visual identity for Valley Strong's home loan program. Valley Strong wanted to reinforce the ease of their program and address anxieties of the home lending process. To address this, we created an identity that focused around a "roof over your head". The visual identity was designed to convey domestic comfort and excite home owners about what's possible with a new home. Creative Director: Summer Woodward Copywriter: Dana Tiel Design assistance: Chantal Herrera

paragraph: When I started working at Meaningful Works, my first assignment was to create a visual identity for Valley Strong Credit Union's home loan program. The challenge in this was that a home loan is not an exciting thing on its surface. The idea of going through a loan of any sort can leave people feeling nervous, anxious, or just uninterested overall. The breakthrough moment in the project came when we turned a source of anxiety into a source of excitement. After all, with a home loan comes a new house.

With this new reframing of a home loan as an exciting path to a new house, creating a visual identity became much easier. We framed the identity around houses, be it short, tall, or wide. These minimalistic houses allowed the user to imagine themselves inside these new spaces, supported by the green colors of Valley Strong Credit Union. To make the metaphor of a house more apparent, roof textures were added to suggest architectural styles. Through play, excitement, and levity, a home loan was no longer a source of anxiety, but a path to an exciting future.

This page contains various projects that either showcase student work during my Graduate Graphic Design program at ArtCenter, or other organizations I worked with. My time at ArtCenter resulted in my graduate thesis Forced Perspective: An Exhibit on Brand. This project was focused around creating artwork that commented on branding and its ability to alter our understanding of the world. The artwork and experience was cataloged in a 300 page book written by myself. Other student projects include California State Parks, a branding project that brought old frontier graphics into playful contemporary design, and THE TRADE SHOW!, a mock art catalog of artists who focus on Capitalism in their work.

This page also includes intern work, such as various projects during my time with Disney's Yellow Shoes, the company's internal marketing firm for Disney Experiences. I also had the opportunity to update KDI's visual identity and create a new visual identity for a Hollywood startup called 10 By Ten Entertainment. There's been many projects I've worked on and there's many more left to do.
